system: recombinant human DYRK1A (Q13627) in vitro kinase reaction with peptide substrate and ATP
readout: ADP-Glo luminescence proportional to ADP produced (inversely proportional to kinase activity)

steps.instruction: Prepare a serial dilution of CHEMBL1077347 in assay buffer with constant vehicle, plus vehicle-only, no-enzyme, no-compound (100% activity), and no-substrate/background controls; include a reference inhibitor if available.

parameters.top_concentration_uM: 30 (assumption: contextual DYRK1A inhibitors span ~0.007–2.1 µM in retained examples CHEMBL4266682/CHEMBL1806286, so 30 µM should bracket full response; not a potency estimate for CHEMBL1077347)
parameters.vehicle_fraction: unresolved — maximum tolerated DMSO fraction for this kinase/ADP-Glo system not stated in packet; keep constant across all wells and verify no interference

steps.instruction: Combine compound dilutions with DYRK1A, peptide substrate, and ATP; preincubate compound with enzyme before initiating with ATP/substrate; run under linear, substrate-non-depleting conditions.

parameters.enzyme_concentration: unresolved — no packet value; must be titrated to give <10–20% ATP consumption in linear range
parameters.substrate_concentration: unresolved — no packet value; a DYRK1A peptide substrate is supported by example CHEMBL2394351 (YRASPSRPESPRPPA-NH2) but concentration is not given
parameters.ATP_concentration: unresolved — no packet value; note example CHEMBL3105981 indicates ATP-competitive behavior for some DYRK1A inhibitors, so ATP choice (e.g., near Km) should be justified experimentally
parameters.reaction_time: unresolved — example CHEMBL2394351 used 10 min preincubation for a different assay format; confirm linearity by time-course
parameters.temperature: unresolved — commonly 25–37 °C but not stated in packet; hold constant and report

steps.instruction: Stop the reaction with ADP-Glo reagent to deplete residual ATP, then add kinase detection reagent and read luminescence.

parameters.reagent_volumes: unresolved — follow vendor protocol; not specified in packet
parameters.depletion_time: unresolved — vendor-typical; not specified in packet
parameters.detection_time: unresolved — vendor-typical; not specified in packet

steps.instruction: Normalize luminescence to no-compound (100% activity) and no-enzyme (0% activity) controls; fit percent inhibition vs log10 concentration with a four-parameter logistic model; report IC50 with 95% CI, Hill slope, and replicate scatter.

parameters.acceptance_criteria: unresolved — set from pilot Z' factor (>0.5), DMSO tolerance, and linear-range ATP consumption (<20%); no packet values

controls: No-enzyme / no-substrate background (defines 0% activity and luminescence floor)
Reference DYRK1A inhibitor (if available) as positive control
Compound-only wells without enzyme to detect luminescence quenching/enhancement by CHEMBL1077347
ATP/ADP standard curve to confirm ADP-Glo linearity
rationale: The question asks for biochemical inhibition of purified DYRK1A, so the kinase luminescence cards (kinase-prepare/react/detect) are used and the cell-viability cards are excluded: cell viability would measure general cytotoxicity, not target-specific inhibition. ADP-Glo is a homogeneous luminescent readout compatible with peptide-substrate DYRK1A assays; retained examples (CHEMBL4266682 radiometric, CHEMBL2394351 peptide-substrate, CHEMBL3105981 ATP-competitive) confirm DYRK1A is assayed biochemically with peptide substrate and ATP, supporting format compatibility though not parameter values. The concentration range is chosen to bracket the contextual DYRK1A inhibitor span (~nM to low µM) with margin; it is an assumption, not a potency estimate for CHEMBL1077347, and no IC50 is predicted.
limitations: No IC50 or assay parameters for CHEMBL1077347 exist in the packet; no potency value is predicted.
Enzyme, substrate, and ATP concentrations, reaction time, temperature, vehicle fraction, and detection timings are unsupported by the packet and must be established by pilot titration.
Retained example IC50s are for other compounds and assay formats (radiometric, LDH, filter binding); they justify only format compatibility and range selection, not expected potency.
If ATP is set far above Km, ATP-competitive inhibitors (cf. CHEMBL3105981) may show right-shifted IC50; ATP Km for this construct is unknown.
This biochemical assay measures enzymatic inhibition only; it does not establish cellular activity or target-specific causality in cells.
